text: Benjamini & Hochberg's 1995 method for correcting p-values across many simultaneous statistical tests -- used in virtually every differential expression analysis -- controls the ___ (abbreviated FDR).
explanation: Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) introduced the false discovery rate (FDR) procedure, which controls the expected proportion of false positives among all rejected null hypotheses -- essential when testing thousands of genes simultaneously in RNA-seq differential expression analysis. Without FDR correction or a similarly principled multiple-testing method, the number of false positives balloons as more genes are tested at a fixed per-test significance threshold.
